blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-migration-1 (Account JSON field renamed without a BREAKING mark) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-migration-2 (Irreversible DROP COLUMN with no down migration or backup) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: The public Account JSON field `user_name` becomes `userName`: every existing API consumer reading `user_name` gets a missing field (null/undefined or a deserialization error) as soon as this version is deployed, with no warning. The proposal's release note lists it only as "Changed: Account JSON uses camelCase." Mark it **BREAKING** in the release note with what consumers must do, and give them a transition: serialize both `user_name` and `userName` for a deprecation period (e.g. a second getter field or a custom Serialize), then remove `user_name` in a later release — so old and new consumers work side by side during rollout.
findings.title: Account JSON field renamed without a BREAKING mark

findings.evidence: ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN legacy_email;
findings.recommendation: Running migration 0005 deletes every value still stored in `users.legacy_email` (rows imported in 2023 keep their data even if the column is no longer written), and unlike 0004 (`0004_accounts.down.sql`) there is no `0005_drop_legacy_email.down.sql`, no backup step and no word in the plan on how to recover. Add a backup step (e.g. copy `id, legacy_email` into an archive table or export before dropping) and a down migration that re-adds the column (restoring from the backup), or state in the plan why the data is disposable and how to recover; also list the column removal in the release note.
findings.title: Irreversible DROP COLUMN with no down migration or backup
